condition: drug-induced acute complete urinary retention in an older man unable to urinate for 18 hours after nightly decongestant use
level_rationale: Complete inability to pass any urine for 18 hours in a 76-year-old man who took oral decongestant tablets nightly for 4 nights indicates acute complete drug-precipitated urinary retention requiring immediate hospital urethral catheterization and bladder decompression, whereas noticing a slower urinary stream than usual while taking decongestant pills for 4 nights in the same 76-year-old man warrants a non-emergent outpatient physician evaluation and medication review.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (76-year-old man, taking oral decongestant pills nightly for 4 nights, and 18-hour complete inability to urinate) with a 2-word span difference (13 vs 15 words), 10 shared trailing tokens, and zero cardinal number words or reassurance negatives. Under Rule A first choice and Rule D, changing complete 18-hour inability to urinate in f3 to a slower urinary stream than usual fits 4 nights of alpha-adrenergic decongestant use cleanly while shifting care from emergency hospital catheterization (level 4) to routine outpatient doctor evaluation (level 2).
